---
title: Scenes, diagrams and formulas
objectives:
  - See a named concept scene rendered from plain data, not a recorded file.
  - See a KaTeX formula rendered inline and on its own line.
---

A named scene builds its frames from a few plain values, so it needs no recorded file at all.
This one shows `input()` reading two lines from standard input, one at a time:

<Figure caption="Reading an integer, then a line of three numbers, from standard input.">
  <Scene name="stdin-flow" lines={["3", "10 20 30"]} reads={[{ name: "n", as: "int" }, { name: "row", as: "split" }]} />
</Figure>

A static diagram is one frozen step of a recorded visual, with no player controls:

<Figure caption="The finished route-count table for a 3 × 4 grid, as one still picture.">
  <Diagram frames="visuals/grid-paths.frames.json" preset="small" step={7} />
</Figure>

One step-through for each of the remaining panel visualizers:

<Figure caption="Two pointers close in on a pair with a given sum in a sorted list.">
  <StepThrough frames="visuals/pair-sum.frames.json" />
</Figure>

<Figure caption="Shortest distances from A: the heap always hands back the closest node not yet done.">
  <StepThrough frames="visuals/dijkstra.frames.json" />
</Figure>

<Figure caption="Every call a recursive function makes, as a tree: each call waits for its children.">
  <StepThrough frames="visuals/fib-calls.frames.json" preset="four" />
</Figure>

<Figure caption="Filling a table of route counts one cell at a time.">
  <StepThrough frames="visuals/grid-paths.frames.json" />
</Figure>

<Figure caption="Merging overlapping intervals with a sweep from left to right.">
  <StepThrough frames="visuals/merge-intervals.frames.json" />
</Figure>

<Figure caption="Binary search for the smallest x whose square reaches a target.">
  <StepThrough frames="visuals/first-square.frames.json" />
</Figure>

KaTeX renders inline, such as $O(n \log n)$, and on its own line:

$$
T(n) = 2T(n / 2) + O(n)
$$
